# Svgbob

Svgbob can create a nice graphical representation of your text diagrams.

Svgbob provides a CLI which takes text as an input and creates an SVG image as an output.

## Demo

[**Interactive Demo**](https://ivanceras.github.io/svgbob-editor/)

## What is Svgbob?

Svgbob is a tool that converts ASCII art text diagrams into beautiful SVG graphics. It automatically recognizes shapes, lines, arrows, and text in your ASCII art and renders them as scalable vector graphics.

## Features

- Converts ASCII art diagrams to SVG
- Supports various shapes: rectangles, circles, lines, arrows
- Handles text within diagrams
- Customizable styling via legends
- Command-line interface for easy integration
- Server mode available for REST API usage

## Usage Examples

### Basic ASCII Art to SVG

Input:
```
    +------+
    |      |
    +------+
```

### Command Line Options

The CLI tool supports various options:

- `--background <color>` - Set backdrop background color (default: white)
- `--fill-color <color>` - Set fill color for solid shapes (default: black)
- `--stroke-color <color>` - Set stroke color for lines (default: black)
- `--font-family <font>` - Set font family for text (default: arial)
- `--font-size <size>` - Set font size (default: 14)
- `--stroke-width <width>` - Set stroke width for lines (default: 2)
- `--scale <factor>` - Scale the entire SVG by this factor (default: 1)
- `-o, --output <file>` - Output file (default: STDOUT)
- `-s, --inline` - Parse an inline string

### Server Mode

Svgbob can also run as a REST API server. Send ASCII art as a POST request and receive SVG output.

## Specification

For detailed information about the diagram syntax and supported features, see the [Specification](https://ivanceras.github.io/content/Svgbob/Specification.html).

## Used By

- [google/comprehensive-rust](https://github.com/google/comprehensive-rust) via [markdown-svgbob](https://github.com/boozook/mdbook-svgbob)
- [asciidoctor](https://docs.asciidoctor.org/diagram-extension/latest/diagram_types/svgbob/)
- [discourse](https://meta.discourse.org/t/discourse-svgbob/223573)
- [typst/bob-draw](https://typst.app/universe/package/bob-draw/)
- [zola](https://zola.discourse.group/t/diagramming-tool-integrations-plantuml-svgbob-graphviz-etc/269)
- [kroki](https://kroki.io/)

# Svgbob Server

Svgbob Server runs svgbob as a REST API, allowing you to convert ASCII art diagrams to SVG via HTTP requests.

## Usage

Start the server on a specific port and send POST requests with your ASCII art:

```sh
curl -X POST -F 'ascii=o------>' http://localhost:3000 > output.svg
```

The server accepts ASCII art as form data and returns the rendered SVG.

import subprocess, string, sys
def body(inp):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"], input=inp.encode(), capture_output=True)
    out=p.stdout.decode()
    lines=out.splitlines()
    idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if "</defs>" in l]
    body=lines[idx[0]+2:-1] if idx else lines
    return " | ".join(b.strip() for b in body)

chars = "+.,'`< >^vVoO*#:;!\"xX/\\|()[]{}-_~=CT"
for c in chars:
    print(f"\n=== char {c!r} ===")
    for name, inp in [
        ("-c-", f"-{c}-"),
        ("-c", f"-{c}"),
        ("c-", f"{c}-"),
        ("|/c/|", f"|\n{c}\n|"),
        ("c-above", f"\n{c}"), # ignore
        ("vert_c", f"{c}\n|"),
        ("vert_above", f"|\n{c}"),
        ("diag1", f"/{c}"),
        ("diag2", f"{c}/"),
        ("diag3", f"\\{c}"),
        ("diag4", f"{c}\\"),
        ("cc", f"{c}{c}"),
        ("ccc_line", f"{c}{c}{c}"),
        ("spacec", f" {c}"),
        ("_c_", f"_{c}_"),
        ("=c=", f"={c}="),
        ("~c~", f"~{c}~"),
        ("plus_around", f" + \n+{c}+\n + "),
    ]:
        print(f"{name:14} {inp!r:20} -> {body(inp)}")

import subprocess

    return " | ".join(b.strip() for b in lines[idx[0]+2:-1])
chars=". ,'`x+/*()<>v^_-"
# positions: TL (E,S), TR (W,S), BL (N,E), BR (N,W), also cross NSEW via plus neighbors
patterns={
 "TL_E_S": "{c}--\n|",

 "N_W": " + \n+{c} \n",
 "S_E": "\n {c}+\n + ",
 "S_W": "\n+{c} \n + ",
 "E_only": "{c}--",
 "W_only": "--{c}",
 "N_only": "|\n{c}",
 "S_only": "{c}\n|",
 "EW": "-{c}-",
 "NS": "|\n{c}\n|",
 "di_SW": "  \n {c}\n/ ",

 "di_SE": " {c}\n  \\",

}

    for name,pat in patterns.items():
        inp=pat.format(c=c)
        print(f"{name:8} {body(inp)}")

import subprocess, string
def body(inp):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"], input=inp.encode(), capture_output=True)
    out=p.stdout.decode(); lines=out.splitlines()
    idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if "</defs>" in l]
    return " | ".join(b.strip() for b in lines[idx[0]+2:-1])
patterns={
 "EW": "-{c}-",
 "NS": "|\n{c}\n|",
 "E": "{c}--",
 "W": "--{c}",
 "N": "|\n{c}",
 "S": "{c}\n|",
 "NE_SWdiag": "  /\n {c}\n/",
 "NW_SEdiag": "\\  \n {c}\n  \\",
 "cross+": " + \n+{c}+\n + ",
 "diagcross": "\\ /\n {c} \n/ \\",
}
for c in string.ascii_letters+string.digits+"!\"$%&?@[]{};:":

        outs.append(f"{name}={'TEXT' if c in b and '<text' in b else b[:120]}")
    # print only if any pattern not simply text?
    print(f"{c!r}: "+" || ".join(outs))

    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"], input=inp.encode(), capture_output=True)
    out=p.stdout.decode(); lines=out.splitlines()
    idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if "</defs>" in l]
    return " | ".join(b.strip() for b in lines[idx[0]+2:-1])
patterns={
 "EW": "-{c}-",
 "NS": "|\n{c}\n|",
 "E": "{c}--",
 "W": "--{c}",
 "N": "|\n{c}",
 "S": "{c}\n|",
 "NE_SWdiag": "  /\n {c}\n/",
 "NW_SEdiag": "\\  \n {c}\n  \\",
 "cross+": " + \n+{c}+\n + ",
 "diagcross": "\\ /\n {c} \n/ \\",
}
for c in string.ascii_letters+string.digits+"!\"$%&?@[]{};:":
    outs=[]
    for name,pat in patterns.items():
        b=body(pat.format(c=c))
        # Determine if c rendered as text (escaped variations)
        txt = f">{c}<" in b or f">{c}" in b  # crude
        outs.append(f"{name}={'TEXT' if c in b and '<text' in b else b[:120]}")
    # print only if any pattern not simply text?
    print(f"{c!r}: "+" || ".join(outs))

python3 /tmp/letters.py > /tmp/letters.txt 2>&1; wc -l /tmp/letters.txt; sed -n '1,40p' /tmp/letters.txt

cat > /tmp/quad.py << 'PY'
import subprocess, string
def body(inp):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"], input=inp.encode(), capture_output=True)
    out=p.stdout.decode(); lines=out.splitlines()
    idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if "</defs>" in l]
    return " | ".join(b.strip() for b in lines[idx[0]+2:-1])

templates={
 "TL": " {X}-\n(",
 "TR": "-{X}\n  )",
 "BL": "(\n {X}-",
 "BR": "  )\n-{X}",
}
for name,pat in templates.items():
    print(f"\n== {name} {pat!r}")
    for x in ". ,'`~!;:()<>^v/*oO+#-_|=":
        b=body(pat.format(X=x))
        # only print if a path with A 20 or 16 and no text for x?
        print(f"{x!r} -> {b}")
PY
python3 /tmp/quad.py > /tmp/quad.txt 2>&1; grep -E "A (20|16|12)" /tmp/quad.txt | head -n 80

import subprocess
def hasbig(inp):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"],input=inp.encode(),capture_output=True)
    return "A 20,20" in p.stdout.decode()
# Represent each pattern by cells dict relative to an anchor. Put pattern on a 9x7 canvas at offset (3,2).
patterns={
 "NW": {(1,0):'.',(2,0):'-',(0,1):'('},
 "NE": {(0,0):'-',(1,0):'.',(2,1):')'},
 "SW": {(0,0):'(',(1,1):'`',(2,1):'-'},
 "SE": {(2,0):')',(0,1):'-',(1,1):"'"},
}
for name,cells in patterns.items():
    ox,oy=3,2
    W,H=9,7
    blockers=[]
    for y in range(H):
     for x in range(W):
        g=[[' ']*W for _ in range(H)]
        for (dx,dy),ch in cells.items(): g[oy+dy][ox+dx]=ch
        if g[y][x]!=' ': continue
        g[y][x]='a'
        inp="\n".join("".join(r) for r in g)
        if not hasbig(inp): blockers.append((x-ox,y-oy))
    print(name,"blockers relative:",blockers)
PY
python3 /tmp/quadblock2.py

import subprocess
def order(inp):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"],input=inp.encode(),capture_output=True)
    body=p.stdout.decode().split("</defs>")[-1]
    seq=[]
    for l in body.splitlines():
        l=l.strip()
        if l.startswith('<line'): seq.append('L')
        elif l.startswith('<path'): seq.append('A')
        elif l.startswith('<text'): seq.append('T('+(l.split('>')[1][:3])+')')
        elif l.startswith('<g'): seq.append('G')
        elif l.startswith('</g'): seq.append('/G')
        elif l.startswith('<rect') and 'backdrop' not in l: seq.append('R')
        elif l.startswith('<circle'): seq.append('C')
        elif l.startswith('<polygon'): seq.append('P')
    return seq
for t in [
